title: Rheostat events are calling preventDefault where the events are not marked with passive=false
body:
## 🐛 Bug description

<!-- A clear and concise description of what the bug is. -->

## 🔍 Bug reproduction

I am getting a browser intervention report:

```
  "id": "PreventDefaultPassive",
  "columnNumber": 190798,
  "lineNumber": 2,
  "message": "Unable to preventDefault inside passive event listener due to target being treated as passive. See https://www.chromestatus.com/features/5093566007214080",
  "sourceFile": "https://steamdb.info/static/js/vendor/algolia-instantsearch.js?v=0a1645e134c5aee5"
```

From a cursory look, it looks like touch events in `components/Slider/Rheostat.js` are being cancelled. Chrome made these events passive by default: https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2017/01/scrolling-intervention

## Environment

- OS: Windows 10
- Browser: Chrome 88
- Version: 4.10.0

comments.body: This component is a fork of https://github.com/airbnb/rheostat/, where I see [no issues](https://github.com/airbnb/rheostat/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+passive) around this yet. Is this behaviour new @xPaw ?

I doubt it's new since last commit to that file was on Oct 8, 2019.

Seems like they have a PR that would fix it: https://github.com/airbnb/rheostat/pull/269

I meant that the behaviour of passive event listeners in Chrome, the rheostat code has indeed not really changed in a while. I have the same question as mentioned in the PR though; as far as I can tell, marking events as passive, or not as passive isn't backwards compatible

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/EventTarget/addEventListener#browser_compatibility
Take a look at "Form with options object supported", are there older browsers that you need to support?
Yes, IE11 is supported by InstantSearch.js @xPaw
Are touch events going to be used in IE11 tough? There's likely a way to feature detect whether options param can be passed.
This issue is a duplicate of #2578
